regionalNotesEnglish: Qualified falling-object and exclusion-zone safety review is required before release; warning tape, a hard hat and a shouted warning are not sufficient controls by themselves.
France/Québec terminology for tear-off, debris chute and exclusion area requires regional roofing review.

sourceDecisionQuestions.question: Exclusion area, warning tape and debris chute need site-specific control and French trade senses. The source tells the crew to put tape around an area but does not establish that tape alone is an approved barrier. Resolve the applicable falling-object control with a qualified roofer/safety reviewer before selecting a command.

Tear-off/démontage and archived dépose need a specific demolition scope. The source scene resumes only after the foreman speaks with the ground crew; archived speaking adds a separate stop-work and approved-zone step. Keep those additions as evidence rather than source-equivalent learner instructions.

Ground crew clear of falling debris and no standing under the work even with a hard hat are the source's safety sequence. Archived zone de travail may broaden the location. Confirm command, exclusion boundary and hard-hat sense in context; do not imply PPE makes overhead work safe.

Source Wait until I say it's clear assigns the release statement to the speaker. Archived French changes this to confirmation that the zone is clear. Determine who is authorized to release the area and preserve that speaker/clearance meaning consistently across card, Reader, speaking and future audio.

Source Heads up! Debris coming down! is an immediate falling-debris alert. Archived French uses a future va/vont tomber; review urgency and whom to warn, while preserving the conditional chute setup and warning-before-use sequence.
